messages:
anika: Heads-up — I ran the new reranker build (rdrk-v2-int8) across the small BEIR slice and seeing ~1.2% absolute NDCG@10 drop vs fp16. Curious if this is quantization noise or dataset/formatting mismatch. anyone seen similar?
liam: did you run with the same tokenizer & doc truncation? small changes there shift ppl a lot.
anika: yeah same tokenizer, same truncation (512). eval command: `python eval/rerank_eval.py --model rdrk-v2-int8 --dataset beir --split test --trunc 512 --batch 128`
maya: can you paste the exact metric output? single number isn't super actionable.
anika: full snippet: `NDCG@1: 0.486 -> 0.478, NDCG@10: 0.612 -> 0.600, MRR: 0.701 -> 0.693` (fp16 -> int8).
tony: small, but consistent. first check: seed/ordering? bootstrap CI will tell if it's statistically significant.
liam: also check per-query delta distribution: maybe a tiny subset of queries tank and drag aggregate down. run: `--per_query_diffs out.csv`
anika: ran that — median delta ~-0.003, but 5% of queries have >0.05 drop. those seem to be long, multi-paragraph queries.
maya: aha. that suggests length or kv-cache differences. int8 runtime may be truncating or altering attention behavior for long contexts. can you repro on fp16 with shorter truncation to isolate?
anika: I ran fp16 with trunc=256 and saw similar degradation on those long queries (NDCG drop concentrated there).
liam: sounds like the model is sensitive to effective context preserved. another axis: doc formatting/whitespace. were documents normalized (newline collapse, html stripped)? small tokenization drift can hurt rerank.
anika: dataset preprocessing was the usual beir pipeline: simple html strip + whitespace collapse.
tony: two-pronged plan: 1) compute bootstrap 95% CI for NDCG/MRR to confirm true regression. 2) do slice-level eval: short (<=16 tokens), mid (17-64), long (>64) queries; also break by doc length and by source (MS MARCO vs TREC).
maya: I can run the bootstrap job on k8s. ETA ~45m for 1k resamples on BEIR subset. command I'm using: `python eval/bootstrap_metrics.py --preds preds.jsonl --n 1000 --metric ndcg@10 --out ci.json`
liam: additionally, try quant-aware calibration: run PTQ with activation folding or per-channel scaling for the attention kernels. previous run used naive symmetric int8. that might cause outlier attention weight quant error on long queries.
anika: noted. quick check: how do folks feel about raising the alert threshold? current CI alert triggers on >=0.5% absolute ndcg drop with p<0.05. this is 1.2% so should fire already but want to make sure we don't churn on noisy slices.
tony: keep alert but add a tag to indicate "slice-driven" vs "global" regression. if slice analysis shows one source causing >0.7 of the drop, label it slice-driven and backlog mitigation.
maya: job results: bootstrap CI for NDCG@10 (fp16 -> int8) = [0.604, 0.616] vs [0.594, 0.606] so CIs don't overlap much. p-value ~0.02.
liam: confirmed statistically significant. next: can we run a light A/B with quantized but with per-channel scaling (PTQ-PCS) to see if that restores?
anika: queued PTQ-PCS run (job id: qc-443). also exporting the top-100 per-query ranked lists so we can do manual failure analysis.
maya: for manual review, focus on queries where delta>0.05 and doc position change >=10 ranks. often these are paraphrase-heavy or long code-like queries.
tony: quick reminder: update the regression dashboard with slice breakdown and include example failing pairs (query + fp16 top doc + int8 top doc) so SRE/QA can reproduce.
anika: action items: 1) maya — finish bootstrap & upload CI (in progress). 2) liam — run PTQ-PCS and compare. 3) tony — update dashboard and add slice tag. 4) anika — collect top failure examples and open a short tech note.
liam: will also add a small smoke job to CI that compares per-slice ndcg variance after each quantization change (so we detect brittle slices earlier).
maya: done; uploading results to /runs/qc-443/bench_reports/ (will post link when available). :white_check_mark:
